correctness.rationale: Contract the sum-c matching; the remaining edges have distinct distances p=c−b and q=c−a, with no loops or parallel edges. Contraction preserves cycle rank. In each residue class modulo gcd(p,q), at exactly u+v vertices the reduced two-distance graph is the cycle generated by +u modulo u+v; fewer vertices give an induced forest and more contain the cycle. Thus c+1≤p+q−gcd(p,q), yielding the strict bound on a. Each extension sum d>max(N,2c) adds matching edges with at least one fresh endpoint and preserves the entire prefix; any cycle at infinity would be finite. A repeated positive difference gives a four-cycle, so N−2 opposite-letter positions are impossible for N≥7 because binom(N−2,2)>N. For the count, x=c−b and y=b−a restrict a to 0≤a<x−gcd(x,y) and a≤N−x−y; the baseline a<x contributes N³/12+O(N²). Removed tuples have a=x−t with 1≤t≤gcd(x,y). For d=gcd(x,y), the strip N<2x+y≤N+d only allows 2(x/d)+y/d=floor(N/d)+1 and hence costs O(N) per d≤N. In the core 2x+y≤N, the divisor identity gives the kernel floor((floor(N/d)−1)²/4); its approximation error totals O(N²). Möbius inversion of totient/d² gives (log X)/ζ(2)+O(1), proving the subtraction N² log N/(4ζ(2)) and the stated ratio. The finite graph and arithmetic tests in verify.py and recorded verification_output.txt were inspected, not rerun; they support the discrete checks, not the asymptotic. Theorem E is the correct citation in arXiv:2609.28059v1 and v3; the unversioned current PDF renumbers it Theorem D. Pinning the version would avoid ambiguity.
